question: Does persistent three-turn search create a visible territory, cash, profit, or army advantage at matched own-turn checkpoints, or is its complete-game gain not explained by these coarse state features?
frozen_policies: Exact same routed-v6 direct policy, deterministic whole-turn teacher selection and native three-turn teacher as the source coverage study; no training, action substitution, search tuning, or new maps.
analysis: Record features from the actual root-turn-start observation for both players as root-minus-opponent leads. First reproduce each source game outcome, action count, root-turn count and teacher-turn count exactly. At each checkpoint compare a candidate arm with the zero-percent direct arm only for seed-seat pairs surviving to that checkpoint in BOTH arms; disclose the number excluded and counts for which BOTH seats survive on an independent map. Summarize per-seat and pooled paired feature differences without a causal or significance claim. Give complete-game root-turn and action-count distributions separately.
interpretation_limit: Replay on already inspected maps is a descriptive mechanism audit, not fresh strength evidence, a trained student, terminal credit, Elo, or a causal mediation analysis. Reaching a checkpoint is post-treatment selection. Do not tune any policy or train a value head on this audit. Predeclare fresh disjoint windows before any future policy training.
resources: Heavy replay only SSH server fedora-toolbox, one pinned CPU nice19 with Rayon/BLAS caps, bounded wall time and tiny compressed output. No GPU, no preemption, no remote original-repo edits.
